Eh, I didn't watch the video, but on the question, I really think the price of something should reflect how hard it is to make or acquire. But that's an impossible pipedream. In a perfect world If it's costing 2 million to make a AAA game these days then the price should reflect that based on projected sales.

Yet here we are with many many games that typically run 7-12 hours long that are very expensive or MMO's that run off microtransactions to keep servers up, making money off cosmetic items that take minimal man hours to put together. One has to wonder where the line is. When is a game worth 60$? When is it worth 100$? What about 20$?

I've paid 60$ for games that I've barely gotten 25 hours of playtime in, and I have a game I got for 2.50$ that I played for over 400 hours. All I can really say for sure is that the consumers are the ones who control the market, if gamers are willing to pay microtransactions on top of a paywall (ex: payday 2, possibly overwatch, any game that is buy to play and has DLC) then of course game companies are going to go for it.

Let's say you develop a game and 200,000 people buy it. Then you get one or two artists to make a bunch of new paint jobs for some guns in the game. I'll be generous and say this takes them a week of solid work to make 5 skins, now sell those skins in a pack for 99c. Let's say your artists are both paid 30$ an hour and work 8 hour days in a 5 day week. That would cost you 3,360$. If just a quarter of the people who bought your game buy the pack you'll make 50,000$ for an investment of less than 10%.

If people will buy it, and it will make you more money, why wouldn't you do it?

It's up to consumers to determine what direction video game pricing will go, obviously gamers are willing to pay for DLC because nearly every major release has a DLC plan these days. Obviously gamers are willing to pay more for a game because new releases always seem to be 50-80$.

I don't think companies should be shamed for taking advantage of the fact that people are willing to pay more for extra content. The fact is consumers should be the ones shamed for buying into this stuff. If you don't want DLC plans and microtransaction based games you shouldn't be paying for them. The companies are run by people who just want money, they don't REALLY care about making good games. They want shit that sells. That is it. Yeah sure maybe people working on the project want to make something cool, but in the end, any big name title is run by producers who want MONEY.The consumers decide what will sell, not the companies, the companies are trying to find out what we are willing to pay for, that's the whole point of this seemingly escalating DLC and microtransaction heavy AAA games coming out, if it looks like they are "testing the waters" to see what business model they can get away with, then they probably are.

Personally I think the vast majority of AAA games are a joke. Half of them are sequels trying to cash in on established fanbases, very few big game companies are willing to attempt a new IP unless you're fuckin Blizzard with a convention for your own singular company every year. Small studios are the way to go, but there's a lot of amateurs out there looking to cash in off regurgitated 16bit shit, so it's definitely a minefield.
